Local spatial statistics: hotspots and LISA clusters

geo-local.Rd

Per-site statistics that say where values cluster, adding columns to data:

  • geo_hotspot(): the Getis-Ord \(G_i^*\) statistic (Getis and Ord 1992; Ord and Getis 1995) as a z-score, its two-sided p-value and a class ("hot", "cold" or "not significant"). The site itself is in its own neighbourhood, with binary weights.

  • geo_lisa(): local Moran's \(I_i\) (Anselin 1995) with row- standardised weights, its expectation, variance, z-score and p-value under conditional randomisation (Sokal, Oden and Thomson 1998), and the cluster type ("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High" or "not significant"). With nperm > 0 the p-value comes from conditional permutation instead.

Neighbours are the k nearest sites (default) or all sites within dist metres (great-circle). Values equal spdep::localG() and spdep::localmoran() for the same neighbours.

Many sites are tested at once, so consider adjusting p_value (for example p.adjust(p_value, "fdr")) before reading individual sites.

Usage

geo_hotspot(
  data,
  value,
  lon = lon,
  lat = lat,
  k = 5,
  dist = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05
)

geo_lisa(
  data,
  value,
  lon = lon,
  lat = lat,
  k = 5,
  dist = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  nperm = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of sites with coordinates and a value column, or an sf table (its point coordinates are used).

value

<data-masking> Numeric column to test.

lon, lat

Longitude and latitude columns in degrees (ignored for sf input), giving great-circle distances in metres. For projected coordinates pass an sf table with its CRS: distances are then straight-line distances in the CRS units.

k

Number of nearest neighbours (used when dist is NULL).

dist

Distance band in metres; overrides k.

alpha

Significance level for the class columns.

nperm

geo_lisa() only: number of conditional permutations for the p-value; 0 (default) uses the analytical randomisation variance.

seed

Optional RNG seed for permutations.

Value

data with columns gi_star, p_value and hotspot (geo_hotspot()), or lisa, lisa_expected, lisa_variance, lisa_z, p_value and cluster (geo_lisa()). Rows with a missing value or coordinate get NA. The neighbour definition is in attribute "neighbours".

References

Anselin, L. (1995). Local indicators of spatial association – LISA. Geographical Analysis, 27, 93-115. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1995.tb00338.x

Getis, A. and Ord, J. K. (1992). The analysis of spatial association by use of distance statistics. Geographical Analysis, 24, 189-206. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1992.tb00261.x

Sokal, R. R., Oden, N. L. and Thomson, B. A. (1998). Local spatial autocorrelation in a biological model. Geographical Analysis, 30, 331-354. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1998.tb00406.x

Ord, J. K. and Getis, A. (1995). Local spatial autocorrelation statistics: distributional issues and an application. Geographical Analysis, 27, 286-306. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.1995.tb00912.x

Examples

# The 16 real Mt Wilhelm ant transects (Mottl, Moses and Klimes 2023)
geo_hotspot(png_ants_sites, elevation, k = 3)
#> # A tibble: 16 × 10
#>    site   transect elevation_band elevation   lon   lat baits gi_star p_value
